Send copies of financial statements and the auditor's report to every member and debenture-holder at least 21 days before the general meeting.
Provide at least 21 days' notice for general meetings to members, auditors, and directors; shorter notice is permitted only if 95% of members entitled to vote consent in writing or electronically.
Forward all notices of general meetings to the auditor, who must attend either personally or through an authorized representative to be heard on relevant business.
Authorize a representative via a Board resolution if an investor is a body corporate, granting the representative the right to vote and exercise powers on behalf of the investor at meetings.
Ensure all personal data processing is for a lawful purpose and based on either voluntary consent or legitimate uses.
Provide a clear, plain-language notice to Data Principals before or at the time of seeking consent, including itemized data description, purpose, and mechanisms for rights exercise.
Provide the notice in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution at the Data Principal's option.
Ensure consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, and obtained via clear affirmative action.
Implement a mechanism allowing Data Principals to withdraw consent with the same ease as providing it, and cease processing upon such withdrawal.
Engage Data Processors to process data on your behalf only under a valid contract.
Implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches.
Notify the Board and affected Data Principals in the prescribed manner in the event of a personal data breach.
Erase personal data when consent is withdrawn or the specified purpose is no longer served, unless retention is required by law.
Establish an effective grievance redressal mechanism for Data Principals.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, appoint an India-based Data Protection Officer responsible to the Board of Directors.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, appoint an independent data auditor and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, perform annual audits and impact assessments, submitting reports to the Board.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, perform due diligence on algorithmic software to ensure it does not risk Data Principal rights.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, comply with any government restrictions on transferring specific personal data outside India.
Classify computer programs as 'literary works' for the purpose of copyright protection.
Recognize that the employer is the first owner of copyright for code created by employees in the course of their employment, unless an agreement states otherwise.
Exercise exclusive rights to reproduce, store, adapt, and sell/rent copies of the proprietary computer program.
Execute assignments of copyright in writing, signed by the assignor, identifying the work, rights, duration, and territorial extent.
Note that if a contract does not specify the duration of an assignment, it is deemed to be five years, and if it does not specify territory, it is presumed to be within India.
Note that a computer programme 'per se' is excluded from being considered an invention under the Patents Act.
Issue a bill of supply instead of a tax invoice if supplying exempted services or paying tax under the composition scheme (section 10), unless the value is less than two hundred rupees.
Issue a receipt voucher upon receiving advance payment for any supply of services.
Issue a refund voucher if a receipt voucher was issued for an advance but no subsequent supply is made and no tax invoice is issued.
Register in the State or Union territory from which taxable services are supplied if aggregate turnover exceeds twenty lakh rupees.
Issue a tax invoice for taxable services provided, containing prescribed particulars, within the prescribed period.

Constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) through a written order at every office or unit with the prescribed composition, including a senior woman presiding officer and an external NGO member.
Provide a safe working environment, display penal consequences of sexual harassment, sensitize employees, and provide facilities for the ICC to conduct inquiries.
Ensure all wages are paid to employees, including the employer's ultimate responsibility for payments even if a contractor fails to do so.
Calculate bonuses for employees with monthly wages exceeding 7,000 rupees (or the higher minimum wage) based on that 7,000 rupee (or minimum wage) threshold.
Register and insure all employees in establishments covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act.
Ensure that if an establishment has 20 or more persons, it complies with the Employees' Provident Funds Act; the Commissioner may also apply this to smaller establishments by agreement.

query: we manufacture IoT devices in an SEZ, employ 200 factory workers, collect device telemetry, hold design registrations and are issuing new shares — what laws apply

steps.action: Offer further shares to existing equity shareholders in proportion to their holding, to employees under a stock option scheme, or to other persons via a special resolution with valuation by a registered valuer.
Provide notice for the offer of shares specifying the number of shares and a timeframe between 15 and 30 days for acceptance.
Allow shareholders a right to renounce their offered shares unless the articles of association provide otherwise.
Ensure that if the issue is a private placement, it is offered to an identified group of persons not exceeding fifty, and application money is received via banking channels.
Allot securities within sixty days of receiving application money for private placements.
File a return of allotment with the Registrar whenever share capital is allotted.
Provide a notice to the Data Principal detailing the personal data (telemetry data) to be processed, the specified purpose, and instructions for exercising rights and filing complaints.
Ensure the notice is provided in clear, plain language, is understandable independently of other info, and includes a link or description of how to withdraw consent or exercise rights.
Obtain free, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent through clear affirmative action before processing personal data.
Implement reasonable security safeguards to protect IoT telemetry data and prevent personal data breaches.
Notify the Board and affected Data Principals in the event of a personal data breach.
Erase telemetry data when the specified purpose is no longer being served or upon withdrawal of consent, unless retention is legally required.
Establish an effective mechanism to redress grievances of Data Principals.
Prominently publish contact information for a person or DPO responsible for answering questions about the processing of personal data.
If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India, an independent data auditor, and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments.
If engaging a Data Processor to handle telemetry data, ensure the engagement is governed by a valid contract.
Apply to the Controller for the registration of a new or original design in the prescribed form and manner with the required fee, ensuring the design is not previously published in any country.
Classify the IoT device design into a single prescribed class of articles for registration purposes.

Furnish prescribed representations or specimens of the design to the Controller and mark each article sold with the prescribed registration notification before delivery, to ensure entitlement to damages for infringement.
Apply for a five-year extension of the ten-year copyright period in the prescribed manner and pay the required fee before the initial term expires.
Seek legal remedies or injunctions against any person who applies, imports, or sells the registered design or an imitation of it without consent.

If a registration lapses and is subsequently restored, observe any conditions imposed by the Controller to protect those who used the design during the lapse period, noting that no infringement suits can be brought for acts committed during that period.
Register the SEZ unit as a separate business vertical distinct from other units located outside the Special Economic Zone.
Claim exemptions from customs duties on goods imported into or exported from the SEZ, and excise duty exemptions for goods brought from the Domestic Tariff Area, to carry out authorised operations.
Apply the zero-rated supply status for goods or services supplied to the SEZ unit, and claim a refund of unutilised input tax credit under bond or Letter of Undertaking.

Comply with customs duties (including anti-dumping and countervailing duties) when removing goods from the SEZ to the Domestic Tariff Area based on the rate and valuation in force at the time of removal.
Issue tax invoices containing specific particulars (GSTIN, HSN code, value of supply, tax rates, etc.) for taxable supplies.
Pay an additional 20% income tax on distributed income if the company conducts a buy-back of its own shares, and deposit this tax within 14 days of the payment to shareholders.
